items.front: What are the steps of a discovery call for an enterprise Claude deployment?
items.back: 1) Agenda & roles  2) Business context & KPIs  3) Current process & quantified pain  4) Data: sources, sensitivity, residency, access  5) Constraints: security, compliance (ZDR, region), procurement, integration  6) Success criteria & who owns the eval set  7) Stakeholders & decision process  8) Scoped pilot & next steps, then a written recap.

items.front: Before proposing a solution in discovery, what should you do?
items.back: Play back what you heard in the customer's words (goal, pain, constraints, success metric) and check it's right. Then propose a narrow pilot with an eval set built from their real examples.

items.front: Customer: "Our data can't leave the EU and we need zero data retention." What do you cover?
items.back: Clarify the actual requirement (law, policy, or preference). Walk through the API data-retention / ZDR options, and deploying via cloud platforms (Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS) in their region. Confirm exact terms in writing; don't improvise.

items.front: Workflow vs agent: what's the difference, and which do you start with?
items.back: Workflow: LLMs and tools follow predefined code paths. Agent: the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use. Start with the simplest thing (often a single call or a workflow); use an agent only when the steps can't be predicted and the extra cost/latency/risk is worth it.

items.front: Name the five workflow patterns in 'Building effective agents'.
items.back: Prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer.

items.front: What three principles does 'Building effective agents' give for agents?
items.back: Keep the design simple; make the agent's planning visible (transparency); invest in the agent-computer interface (tool docs and testing).

items.front: How would you tier current Claude models in a customer architecture?
items.back: Haiku 5.5 for high-volume, low-latency steps (routing, classification). Sonnet 5.5 for a speed/intelligence balance. Opus 5.5 is the recommended starting point for most workloads. Fable 5.1 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Choose per step using evals and cost.

items.front: What is Contextual Retrieval and how much did it help?
items.back: Prepend chunk-specific context (explaining where the chunk sits in its document) before embedding and BM25 indexing. It cut top-20 retrieval failures by 49% (contextual embeddings + contextual BM25), and by 67% with reranking.

items.front: How do you enforce role-based access in an enterprise RAG system?
items.back: Store source ACLs as metadata on every chunk, sync them from the source systems, and filter at retrieval time using the user's SSO identity (not a shared service account). Add leakage tests with users of different roles to the eval set, and audit-log queries and returned documents.

items.front: Tool design tips from 'Writing effective tools for agents'?
items.back: Choose a few deliberate, task-shaped tools (not a wrapper per API endpoint); namespace them (e.g. crm_search, erp_get_order); return high-signal, compact context; and test tools with evals.

items.front: What's a safe rollout sequence for an enterprise LLM feature?
items.back: Pilot with a small group and an eval set, then shadow mode (model runs alongside humans, outputs compared, not acted on), then staged launch by group or category. Add monitoring, cost controls and a feedback loop into the eval set.

items.front: Where do human checkpoints belong in an agent design?
items.back: Before irreversible or high-impact actions (sending to customers, payments, writes to systems of record, parts orders), and as escalation for low confidence or out-of-scope cases. Log every approval.

items.front: How much do prompt-cache reads cost, and when do you use caching?
items.back: Cache reads cost 10% of the base input price (5% on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5; 2.5% on Fable 5.1). Use it for long, repeated prefixes: system prompts, tool definitions, policy documents, few-shot examples.

items.front: When do you recommend the Message Batches API, and what does it save?
items.back: For asynchronous, non-latency-sensitive work (overnight extraction, backfills, monthly reports, eval runs). Batches get a 50% discount.

items.front: Context window and max output on current Claude models?
items.back: 1M-token context window and 128K max output tokens on the current models (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5).

items.front: Can you call the Claude API directly from a browser for a customer app?
items.back: Docs recommend a back end. Direct browser calls need the `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true` header and are acceptable only for trusted internal tools or short-lived dev keys. Orgs with ZDR or the Compliance API enabled can't make browser (CORS) calls at all: they get a 401.

items.front: What breaks if you move to `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`?
items.back: The `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` parameters are removed and return a 400 error. Don't send them with that version.

items.front: Structure for presenting a take-home Claude app to a panel?
items.back: 1) Customer problem & success criteria  2) Architecture diagram  3) Prompt & tool design  4) Evals with numbers  5) Failure modes & guardrails  6) Cost & latency (caching, batches, model choice)  7) Next steps with the customer. State assumptions; leave time for Q&A.

items.front: May you use Claude while building Anthropic's take-home?
items.back: Not unless Anthropic says otherwise. Take-homes are done without Claude unless indicated, and live interviews are 'all you'. Using Claude to prepare is encouraged.

items.front: How do you build an eval harness with a customer?
items.back: Define success criteria with the customer; build a golden set from real cases (agents: start with 20-50 tasks from real failures); pick graders: code where possible, LLM judges calibrated against humans, human review; grade outcomes rather than paths; rerun on every prompt/model change; watch for saturation.

items.front: Three kinds of graders for LLM evals, and a trade-off for each?
items.back: Code-based (fast, cheap, objective, but only for checkable outputs); model-based / LLM judge (flexible for open-ended outputs, must be calibrated against human labels); human (gold standard, slow and expensive, use for calibration and spot checks).

items.front: Current RSP version, and what triggers stronger safeguards?
items.back: RSP v3.4, effective 2026-07-08. Capability thresholds trigger stronger ASL safeguards. The ASL-3 deployment standard is defense in depth: access controls, real-time classifiers, async monitoring, jailbreak rapid response.

items.front: Core Views on AI Safety in one sentence?
items.back: Transformative AI may arrive within about a decade and nobody yet knows how to make it reliably safe, so Anthropic does empirical safety research on frontier systems with a portfolio approach across optimistic, intermediate and pessimistic scenarios.

items.front: Which hiring-manager questions were reported on Glassdoor for Anthropic SA roles?
items.back: Why you want to join; your views on Anthropic's research papers; and (one candidate) whether you'd be fine if the stock went to zero.
